questions.q: State the basic properties of a magnet.
answer: A magnet shows several definite properties.

answer.text: It attracts magnetic materials such as iron, nickel and cobalt, but not non-magnetic materials like wood, plastic or paper.
Every magnet has two poles, north and south, and its pulling force is strongest at the poles. The poles always exist in pairs — breaking a magnet gives smaller magnets, each with both poles.
Like poles repel each other and unlike poles attract; repulsion is the sure test of a magnet.
A freely suspended magnet always comes to rest in the north–south direction.

questions.q: How does a magnetic compass work, and how can a magnet be made?

answer.text: A compass contains a small, freely pivoted magnetic needle. Because a freely suspended magnet always settles in the north–south direction, the needle points north, letting us find directions. This works because the Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet.
An ordinary iron bar can be turned into a magnet by stroking it many times in the same direction with one pole of a bar magnet, lifting the magnet away at the end of each stroke.
Magnets lose their power if heated, hammered or dropped, so bar magnets are stored in pairs with unlike poles together and kept away from electronic devices.

questions.q: Distinguish between magnetic and non-magnetic materials, with examples.

answer.text: Magnetic materials are those that are attracted by a magnet. Iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic materials, and objects made from them, such as iron nails, pins and steel articles, are pulled towards a magnet.
Non-magnetic materials are those that are not attracted by a magnet. Substances like wood, plastic, paper, cloth, rubber and aluminium are non-magnetic, and a magnet has no effect on them.

We can find out whether a material is magnetic by bringing a magnet near it and seeing whether it is attracted. This property is even used to separate magnetic substances, such as iron, from a mixture.

answer: Thus magnetic materials like iron are attracted by a magnet, while non-magnetic materials like wood and plastic are not.

questions.q: How should magnets be stored and cared for, and what can weaken a magnet?

answer.text: A magnet does not keep its power for ever. It can become weak and lose its magnetism if it is not handled and stored properly.
Heating a magnet strongly, hammering or dropping it repeatedly, and leaving bar magnets carelessly together can all weaken it. Magnets should therefore be handled gently and kept away from heat.

Bar magnets should be stored in pairs, placed side by side with unlike poles facing opposite ends, and separated by wooden spacers, with soft iron pieces called keepers across the ends. A horseshoe magnet is stored with a keeper across its poles.

answer: Thus, to keep magnets strong, we must protect them from heat and rough handling and store them correctly with keepers.
